_comment: Example critical journey (ARCHITECTURE §8.2, journey.schema.json) for a fictional bicycle-parts inventory. Save real journeys as .ui-evaluator/journeys/<id>.json, one per critical or core task in PRODUCT.md. `uie journey <id>` replays correct_actions and checks success_condition (FUN-03). The walkthrough evaluator treats each action as one step and asks the four questions of METHODS §4.2 for the persona. Fields without their own note: id (the file name, lowercase words joined by hyphens), title (the task, verb first), goal (what the persona wants, in their own terms). Keys starting with _ are notes for people. Never put passwords or real personal data in a journey.
title: Record a delivery of parts
_criticality: critical | core | peripheral, from the task's rank in PRODUCT.md. Peripheral journeys cap their findings at P2 (FRAMEWORK §4.5).
_frequency: frequent (several times a day) | regular (weekly) | occasional (a few times a year) | rare (once or twice). Used to rank journeys and by the motion frequency budget.

persona._comment: Built from a user group in PRODUCT.md. knows and does_not_know drive the walkthrough's questions about whether the user will try, notice and connect the right action.
persona.group: Workshop staff who unpack supplier deliveries
knows: part numbers as printed on delivery notes
which supplier each box comes from
how to use the shared workshop laptop
does_not_know: the inventory's own word for adding received stock
whether a delivery must match an order first
persona.context: Standing at the workbench with the open box; the laptop is shared and interruptions are common

goal: Make the shop's records match what has just arrived, so the parts can be sold today
scenario: A box from your brake supplier has just arrived. The delivery note lists 12 sets of disc brake pads, part number BP-2207. Make sure the shop's records show that these 12 sets are now on the shelf.
_scenario: Written for a person, with every detail needed and no words from the interface (no labels, menu names or icons). Task cards for user tests start from this text.

start_state._comment: Where replay starts and what must exist first. Sign-in comes from a stored session or a seeded test account in the project's fixtures, never from credentials in this file.
start_state.data: part BP-2207 exists with 3 sets on hand; no open deliveries

success_condition._comment: Observable and checkable by script; every predicate in all must hold after the last action. A predicate has a url (regular expression), or text with an optional target locator, or a target with a state.

_correct_actions: The one correct path, fixed before anyone walks it (METHODS §4.2). Actions: goto {url}; click {target}; fill {target, value}; press {key, optional target}; expect {text with optional target, or url, or target with state: visible, hidden, enabled, focused}. Targets are Playwright-style locators; prefer role plus accessible name, so replay also checks that controls are named.
